strengths: The paper addresses an important practical problem: distilling high-resolution classification datasets without expensive bilevel optimization. Combining classwise feature representatives with per-class BatchNorm statistics gives a straightforward pipeline that scales to ImageNet-1K.

The reported results are promising. At 50 images per class, WMDD achieves 59.4% on Tiny ImageNet and 57.6% on ImageNet-1K, compared with CDA's 48.7% and 53.5%, respectively (Table 1). These are substantial improvements.

Evaluation covers three datasets, multiple compression budgets, three-run averages, component ablations, and regularization sensitivity. Transfer within the ResNet family is encouraging: ImageNet-1K data distilled using ResNet-18 achieve 62.2% with ResNet-101 at 50 images per class (Table 2).

The high-level pipeline is clearly presented, and the manuscript credits SRe2L, the existing barycenter algorithm, datasets, and software dependencies. The supplementary discussion appropriately acknowledges dependence on pretrained classifiers and the possibility of preserving dataset biases.
weaknesses: The central novelty is insufficiently established. For the squared Euclidean cost used here, optimizing both support locations and unrestricted probability weights against one empirical distribution reduces Eq. (7) to the k-means quantization objective: the average squared distance to the nearest representative. The paper neither discusses this equivalence nor compares against feature-space k-means followed by the same image recovery procedure. Figure 1's illustration of barycenters across multiple distributions does not establish an advantage beyond clustering in the actual formulation.

The connection between the optimized distribution and the delivered dataset is incomplete. Algorithm 2 learns nonuniform weights, but Algorithm 1 returns only images, and Eqs. (16)–(18) do not specify how those weights enter sampling or downstream training. Matching support locations alone does not reproduce the optimized weighted distribution. Clarifying this mechanism and comparing learned versus uniform weights are necessary to support the distribution-matching interpretation.

The experiments do not convincingly attribute the headline gains to Wasserstein matching. Holding cross-entropy and per-class BatchNorm fixed, adding the barycenter loss changes ImageNette accuracy from 64.0% to 63.9%, Tiny ImageNet from 41.3% to 42.1%, and ImageNet-1K from 37.4% to 37.9% (Table 3). Moreover, the ImageNet-1K baseline at 10 images per class is 21.3% in Table 1 but 36.1% in Table 3, without a clear reconciliation. Matched training protocols and ablations at the higher budgets are needed to establish the contribution's magnitude.

The MMD comparison does not isolate the distance metric. Section 5.5 removes augmentations and FKD but does not establish identical feature extractors and BatchNorm regularization. At one image per class, the squared-Wasserstein representative is simply the feature mean, also the target of linear mean matching under a common fixed feature map. Consequently, the 0.48% versus 5.77% result cannot establish the claimed geometric advantage without additional controls. The discussion also conflates limitations of linear mean matching with MMD generally.

The solver description contains substantive inconsistencies. The Hessian 2w_jI describes the quadratic with a fixed transport plan; it does not establish convexity of the optimized Wasserstein objective in support locations. Algorithm 2 updates weights and then reuses the previous transport plan without explaining how marginal consistency is restored. It also permits zero weights despite subsequent inverse-weight updates. These issues require clarification, alongside the unspecified barycenter initialization, iteration count, and learning-rate settings.

The efficiency evidence is too narrow for the scalability claims. Table 6 measures ImageNette at one image per class, where computing the representative reduces to a mean. It does not establish transport-solver costs at larger budgets on ImageNet-1K or clearly account for teacher training, feature extraction, and relabeling. End-to-end timing and memory measurements would make the practical efficiency claim substantially more convincing.
